correctness.rationale: The final claim accurately describes the full-dimensional Euclidean chainlink polytope for s≥2, positive integer a_i, l≥0, and 2l≤min a_i. The coordinate facets have normals of length 1 and the directed-difference facets normals sqrt(2), so a radius-rho inscribed ball requires rho≤x_i≤a_i−rho and x_i−x_{i+1}≤a_i−l−sqrt(2)rho. Let y_i=x_i−rho. The potential constraints correspond exactly to graph edges 0→i of weight a_i−2rho, i→0 of weight 0, and i+1→i of weight a_i−l−sqrt(2)rho. Standard no-negative-cycle potential feasibility holds in both directions (shortest paths yield potentials). The only simple cycles are hub cycles with ring path length m−1, weight sum_I a−(m−1)l−rho[2+(m−1)sqrt(2)], and the full ring with weight sum_i a_i−sl−s sqrt(2)rho. These are necessary and sufficient, yielding (5); normalized H constraints at rho=r give all centers. A zero cycle sums nonnegative facet slacks to zero, so its constituent facets are tangent. For uniform a, the interval barrier is (a+q(a−l))/(2+q sqrt(2)), monotone in q≥0; including the full ring reduces r to min(a/2,(a−l)/sqrt(2)). In the strict box case c=a/2 unique; in strict link case c=t·1 with r≤t≤a−r. The boundary equal phase has a unique midpoint center as a consequence of box equality. This exact proof is all-dimensional. An independent formulation with scipy.optimize.linprog (HiGHS) matched the formula in 392 distinct deterministic/random admissible cases in dimensions 2–9 to max 8.9e−16; this is corroboration, not proof. The seven-entry source tree was independently SHA-1 reconstructed and matches its assigned ID.

originality.rationale: Although the 2022/2024 source paper introduces chainlink polytopes without an Euclidean inradius calculation, the full alleged theorem is a direct instance of existing minimum-cost-to-time-ratio cycle and potential-feasibility characterizations. For a radius rho, define a graph with 0->i of cost a_i and time 2, i->0 of cost/time 0, and i+1->i of cost a_i-l and time sqrt(2). The Chebyshev radius is the largest rho with a feasible vertex potential, hence precisely the minimum cost/time ratio of its cycles, by Bringmann–Hansen–Krinninger (2017) Lemmas 2 and 4 and standard facet-normal LP. The graph is an obvious directed ring with a hub; its only simple cycles are hub-to-hub cyclic intervals and the full ring, so the claim’s displayed R_{i,m} and R_cyc are immediate evaluations of the established general characterization. The incenter inequality description and zero-cycle tangencies are the same standard feasibility and zero-slack consequences. Thus the exact numerical identities and geometric contact assertions are covered by a routine specialization of stronger general published results, even though the chainlink name is absent. This is substantive prior implication, not rejection from lack of search results or mere algorithmic computability.

value.rationale: The Euclidean inradius and set of maximizing centers are natural realization-sensitive invariants of a canonical, recently introduced poset-related polytope family, with quantification over all dimensions and heterogeneous compositions. The statement provides a useful explicit finite family of inequalities (including genuine proper interval minimizers, e.g. a=(16,32,17), l=6 has minimizing interval i=3,m=2), an exact contact-chain interpretation and a homogeneous qualitative center transition. This packaged geometry can be useful despite being mathematically implied by existing general theory, much as specialized closed-form applications can have expository/reference value. Value PASS does not establish originality or justify acceptance; generic ratio-cycle theory makes the claimed discovery mathematically covered.
